selectionReason: The RWTH source fixes chemistry, lot, temperature, and duty profile across 48 cells, reaches 80% EOL, and measures BOL plus repeated capacity and pulse diagnostics. It directly tests the within-condition frailty bottleneck left open by RC54.
newFacts: All 16 untouched target cells had a registered 80%-of-own-BOL capacity event, providing 77 comparable non-tied pairs.
The baseline held-cell median absolute error was 80.0 cycles; adding the first-RPT capacity response increased it to 90.309 cycles.
Capacity-response concordance was 0.415584, below both chance-like 0.5 and the registered 0.65 gate.
The capacity-response model's maximum calibration error was 0.239076, above the registered 0.15 gate.
The registered 10 ms pulse response is absent: official processed pulse records provide 2-second and 10-second durations, so no substitute was introduced.
Python and a dependency-free Node implementation agreed over 49 scalar comparisons with maximum absolute difference 5.205e-6.

H0.meaning: The registered sparse early responses do not establish stable cell-specific frailty beyond a common-condition lifetime distribution.

H2.reason: No 10 ms pulse-resistance observation exists in the pilot schema; 2-second and 10-second values cannot answer the registered hypothesis.

diagnosis: The first 160-cycle capacity loss occupied a narrow 2.19–3.98% range, while later degradation accelerated at different times.
A weak positive development association did not transfer: response–lifetime Spearman rho changed from 0.369 in development to -0.167 in target.
Alternative modulo splits also missed the 0.65 concordance gate (0.416, 0.568, and 0.244), so the failure is not explained by one unlucky registered residue alone.
The endpoint had only four distinct target times after the landmark because full-capacity RPTs were widely spaced; this limits fine ordering but does not explain a concordance below 0.5.

minimalAcademicAdvance: A single early capacity-fade rate is not a transportable frailty coordinate even when stress, chemistry, and lot are fixed. This separates population lifetime modeling from cell-specific ranking and prevents an apparently plausible development correlation from being promoted into a digital twin.

mostPromisingNextPath.hypothesis: The onset and curvature of the later degradation knee, not the first 160-cycle capacity loss, carries the stable cell-specific signal; a deliberately excited kinetic response may reveal that transition earlier than passive capacity RPTs.
mostPromisingNextPath.differentCombination: Combine interval-censored changepoint inference, multistep current excitation, and hierarchical survival modeling. The changepoint locates transition risk, excitation estimates kinetic state, and the hierarchy keeps stress effects separate from individual frailty.
mostPromisingNextPath.exactBottleneck: Early scalar fade is too narrow and mechanism-ambiguous to order later knee onset among same-condition cells.
mostPromisingNextPath.developmentExperiment: On the RWTH cohort, compare frozen landmarks at 160, 320, and 480 cycles using only pre-landmark capacity curvature and the available 2-second/10-second resistance histories. Use nested cell splits and treat this only as method development because the source has now been opened.
mostPromisingNextPath.independentDecisiveTest: Before opening a new same-condition lot, freeze one landmark and at most three mechanistically named coordinates. Hold out an entire production or test-start batch; require at least 90% coverage, 14 EOL events, 30 comparable pairs, concordance >=0.65, calibration error <=0.15, and independent implementation.
mostPromisingNextPath.requiredSource: At least 36 same-chemistry cells per fixed condition, full-capacity checks no more than 50 cycles apart, raw sub-second pulse or multistep excitation waveforms, randomized tester channels, and follow-up through 80% EOL.
mostPromisingNextPath.successSignal: The same coefficient direction and >=0.65 held-batch concordance reproduce in a new lot without target calibration.
mostPromisingNextPath.rejectionAndStop: Reject a coordinate if its sign changes across internal start cohorts, held-batch concordance is below 0.65, calibration exceeds 0.15, or acquisition coverage falls below 90%. Stop adding model complexity until observability or endpoint resolution improves.
mostPromisingNextPath.failureValue: A failed excitation coordinate still eliminates a proposed state variable and quantifies the minimum landmark or measurement resolution needed for individual RUL.

uncertaintyBudget.observed: Capacity RPTs are separated by about 160 cycles and early loss spans only a few percentage points.
uncertaintyBudget.consequence: Noise and interval quantization can dominate the early slope and tie EOL times.

uncertaintyBudget.observed: One C-grade production lot under one profile; 16 held cells.
uncertaintyBudget.consequence: The negative result is strong for this sparse coordinate in this cohort, not universal across lots or chemistries.

uncertaintyBudget.observed: A linear one-feature Weibull AFT model was frozen and independently reproduced.
uncertaintyBudget.consequence: A nonlinear relationship could exist, but fitting it post hoc to 30 development cells would not be credible confirmation.

uncertaintyBudget.observed: No 10 ms pulse value exists in the official processed pilot records.
uncertaintyBudget.consequence: RC55 cannot accept or reject the registered kinetic-response hypothesis.

safetyEthics: Only public, previously collected cell data were processed. No cell operation, destructive test, personal data, cyber experiment, or deployment decision occurred.
nextCycleStart: Audit independent same-condition datasets for sub-50-cycle full-capacity resolution plus raw sub-second excitation. If none qualifies, preregister the RWTH multi-landmark analysis strictly as method development and publish the acquisition gap instead of relabeling 2-second data as 10 ms evidence.
